options: A data point far from the rest of the dataset
The largest point in the cluster
The middle point of the data
questions.explanation: An outlier is a point that sits unusually far from the other values.
questions.misconception: Neither the largest cluster member nor the middle — the outlier stands apart from the group by distance.

questions.prompt: How do you usually spot an outlier on a plot?
options: It sits away from the cluster with a gap
It is at the graph's center
questions.explanation: The lone point separated by an empty gap from the cluster is the outlier.
questions.misconception: Color, label, and position are not the signal — the visible empty distance is what marks the outlier.

questions.prompt: A huge outlier added to a dataset will...
options: Leave the mean exactly the same
questions.explanation: Adding a huge value to the total raises the mean toward it.
questions.misconception: The mean uses every value including the outlier, so it must move toward it; the median is the statistic that mostly stays put.

questions.prompt: Which becomes the most extreme WHEN the outlier is present?
questions.explanation: The range is max − min, so a far point stretches it dramatically.
questions.misconception: The range only cares about the extremes — an outlier at an end blows it up, while the median ignores it.

questions.prompt: When you find an outlier, the first thing to do is...
questions.explanation: Investigate first — it may be a real rare event or a recording error.
questions.misconception: Deleting or rounding without investigating can lose real information or leave an error distorting your data.
